title: Solar-Powered Smart Mini Cold Storage System for Fresh Vegetables in North Eastern Region (NER)
org: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)
department: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)
description:
Background:
The North Eastern Region (NER) produces a substantial quantity of fresh vegetables and horticultural crops. However, due to inadequate cold storage infrastructure, unreliable electricity supply, difficult terrain, and transportation delays, farmers often face heavy post-harvest losses. Most remote farming areas lack access to affordable small-scale cold storage facilities near production clusters and local markets. As a result, fresh vegetables deteriorate rapidly before reaching consumers, reducing farmer income and affecting supply chain efficiency. There is a need for a low-cost, energy-efficient, and decentralized cold storage solution suitable for rural and remote regions of NER.
Description:
This problem statement seeks the development of a Solar-Powered Smart Mini Cold Storage System for farmers and vegetable producers in the North Eastern Region (NER) to reduce postharvest losses of perishable vegetables. Due to poor cold-chain infrastructure, difficult transportation routes, frequent power cuts, and long travel durations from remote villages to markets, fresh vegetables often spoil within a short time after harvest. Farmers are forced to sell produce at low prices or suffer financial losses due to lack of nearby storage facilities. The proposed system should function as a decentralized mini cold storage unit that can be installed at village-level collection centres, local markets, farmer cooperatives, and farm-gate aggregation points.
The system should:
a. Preserve fresh vegetables such as tomatoes, cabbage, beans, leafy vegetables, chilli, and other horticultural produce under suitable storage conditions b. Operate using solar energy with battery backup support for off-grid and low-electricity areas c. Maintain controlled temperature and humidity levels for extending shelf life of vegetables d. Include smart monitoring features for:
• Temperature fluctuation
• Humidity variation
• Power failure alerts
• Storage condition status e. Be compact, modular, and suitable for deployment in remote hilly terrain and rural agricultural clusters f. Be energy-efficient, weather-resistant, and capable of operating under varying climatic conditions of NER g. Support easy operation and low maintenance for farmer groups, cooperatives, and local vendors h. Help reduce spoilage during temporary storage before transportation to larger markets The solution should strengthen local agricultural supply chains, reduce vegetable wastage, improve market accessibility, and enhance income opportunities for farmers in the North Eastern Region.
Expected Solution:
A functional hardware-based smart mini cold storage system suitable for rural and remote agricultural areas of the North Eastern Region. The proposed solution should include:
a. Solar-powered cooling system with energy-efficient operation b. Insulated cold storage chamber for preserving fresh vegetables and horticultural produce c. Battery backup support for uninterrupted operation during power outages or low sunlight conditions d. Temperature and humidity monitoring mechanism for maintaining suitable storage conditions e. Smart alert/indicator system for:
• Temperature fluctuations
• Power failure
• Unsafe storage conditions f. Compact and modular design suitable for village-level deployment and difficult terrain g. Weather-resistant and durable structure for varying climatic conditions in NER h. Low-maintenance and cost-effective system suitable for farmer cooperatives, local markets, and collection centres i. Basic digital monitoring/display interface for storage status and system performance The solution should help reduce post-harvest vegetable spoilage, improve shelf life of produce, strengthen local cold-chain infrastructure, and enhance income opportunities for farmers in the North Eastern Region.
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a smart vehicles problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (2/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (5/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within Smart Vehicles. Tech Depth (2/5): centers on infrastructure. Sustainability (5/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 19/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Solar-Powered Smart Mini Cold Storage System for Fresh Vegetables in North Eastern Region (NER)

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a small, solar-powered cold storage unit that farmers in remote NER villages can use right where they harvest, so vegetables don't spoil before reaching market.
overview.why_it_matters: Post-harvest loss isn't an abstract inefficiency, it's money straight out of a farmer's pocket. A working village-level cold box changes that math directly.
pain_points: No cold storage near production clusters in remote areas.
Unreliable grid power makes conventional refrigeration unviable.
Farmers forced to sell at low prices immediately or lose produce to spoilage.
overview.background: NER produces significant fresh vegetable volume but lacks cold-chain infrastructure, and unreliable electricity plus difficult terrain make conventional cold storage impractical at the village level.
overview.whats_being_asked: A decentralized, solar-powered, small-scale cold storage unit deployable at village collection points, energy-efficient and low-cost.
expected_solution: Energy-efficiency validated against actual cooling load.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Incremental. Solar cold storage is an established technology category, the innovation here is in cost/efficiency optimization for this specific rural NER context, not a new concept.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Low. This is a physical build with well-understood components (solar panel, battery, insulated chamber, cooling unit), the challenge is optimization and cost, not novel engineering.

competitive_landscape.note: Hardware-heavy agri-infrastructure PS draw fewer software-first teams, a genuinely less-contested lane if your team can build physically.

innovation.note: Solar cold storage exists in various forms already, the value here is practical optimization, not novelty.

invention.note: Straightforward components, the effort is in sizing and integration, not invention.

technical_feasibility.tag: Tight for a full working unit, workable for a scaled-down demo
technical_feasibility.note: A genuinely functional cold storage prototype in 36 hours is ambitious, a scaled-down proof-of-concept is realistic.

impact_and_benefits.note: Post-harvest loss reduction has an immediate, quantifiable income impact for farmers, very concrete impact story.

architecture.note: Solar + battery + insulated chamber + basic cooling, a single physical system, not a complex data pipeline.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow, undersold by low innovation/scalability scores, but genuinely buildable and high-impact for a hardware-capable team. The low crowding is a real advantage.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Concrete, provable value: measure temperature inside vs. outside the unit, and the demo argues for itself.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: A full-size, market-ready cold storage unit isn't achievable in 36 hours, teams need to commit early to a scaled-down but genuinely working demo.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm access to basic components (solar panel, battery, insulation material, small cooling unit like a Peltier module) before committing, this is a materials-dependent build.

idea_0_4: Scope to a scaled-down demo unit, not a full-size deployable one, decide the target size now.
Choose your cooling method: Peltier (simpler, less efficient) vs. compressor-based (harder, more realistic at scale), pick based on team skill and materials access.
Source materials immediately, this PS is materials-gated more than most.
prototype_4_22: Build the insulated chamber and cooling system first, this is the core physical deliverable.
Wire in the solar/battery power system.
Start instrumenting temperature logging so you have real data to show.
integration_22_30: Get the full solar-to-cooling loop running end to end.
Log real temperature-over-time data, this becomes your key evidence.
Test under a simulated off-grid scenario (disconnect from any backup power).
polish_30_36: Prepare a clear before/after: unrefrigerated produce vs. produce in your unit, if time allows even a short real test.
Build a simple cost/efficiency summary for the scale-up case.
Rehearse leading with the farmer income story, then show the physical unit.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show a live temperature graph from your actual unit running during the demo, real sensor data beats a claimed spec sheet every time on a hardware PS.

strengths: Low crowding, low technical complexity relative to other PS, genuinely achievable in 36 hours.
Extremely concrete and provable impact story.
weaknesses: Materials-dependent build, real risk if components aren't sourced fast.
Low innovation ceiling means differentiation has to come from execution quality, not concept.

roles_needed: One person on data logging and cost analysis
team_fit.ideal_ratio: Hardware-skill-heavy, at least two people comfortable with physical build and wiring.
team_fit.approach: Source materials in the first hour, in parallel with any planning, this is the actual bottleneck.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The cost/efficiency analysis writeup and any data-logging dashboard.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Sizing the cooling system correctly for the insulation and chamber volume, this is physics/engineering judgment, not something an AI tool computes for you reliably without real inputs.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-suggested component list without actually testing the thermal math will likely under- or over-spec the cooling system, and that failure only shows up when you test it.

data_resource_availability.status: No dataset dependency, resourcing risk is physical materials, not data.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If full solar integration isn't possible in time, demo the cooling chamber on grid power with a clear explanation of the solar sizing calculation as a planned addition.

judge_qna.question: What's your actual measured cooling performance, not the theoretical spec?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Show your logged temperature data over the test period, with ambient temperature for comparison, real numbers, not a datasheet claim.
judge_qna.follow_up: How does performance change on a cloudy day with reduced solar input?

judge_qna.question: What does this cost to deploy at a village collection point, and who pays for it?
judge_qna.strong_answer: State your actual component cost total and reference how this could fit into existing agri-infrastructure subsidy schemes.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the maintenance burden on a village-level operator?
